subject: SPECIAL-NAMES paragraph
notes: Rule (cite.py --check 12.3.7.4 "the functionality of the characters used to represent the decimal separator and the grouping separator are exchanged" -> OK §12.3.7.4 14)): a) numeric literals use comma as decimal separator; b) basic-format PICTURE writes and inserts comma as decimal separator and period as grouping separator; locale-format PICTURE unaffected ("The DECIMAL-POINT IS COMMA clause has no effect on the editing or de-editing of a data item described with the locale format of the PICTURE clause" -> OK); NOTE 4 - not applied to literals in compiler directives. Measured (probe/snp3/g14.cob at 2023, g14b.cob at --std 85): MOVE 1,5 TO 9V9 -> 15; COMPUTE 1,5 + 1,5 -> 30 (3.0); ADD 1, 2 (comma+space separator) -> 03; VALUE 3,25 -> 325; PIC 9.999,99 <- 1234,5 -> '1.234,50'; PIC ZZZ.ZZ9,99- <- -1234,5 -> '  1.234,50-'; de-edit 1.234,50 -> 9(4)V99 123450; >>DEFINE KV AS 2.5 with >>IF KV > 2 -> true (the directive literal keeps the period, NOTE 4). Both halves verified at 85 and 2023; the locale-format half is golden-pinned by pb64t6_locale_edit_dpc (byte-identical to the non-DPC sibling). PB616 (open) owns the inherited '§12.3.7 GR14a' miscitation at ~11 code sites for this rule - a citation defect, not a behavior one; referenced, not re-reported. [registrar 14a — editions as adjudicated: 85, 2002, 2014, 2023 (the locale-format PICTURE sentences and NOTE 3 from 2002, with PICTURE format 2)]
